SOURCE.DESCRIPTION:
W_USER_D dimension table contains information about users who created or modified records in the source system, from which the rows have been extracted. It has the contact and location information about the users. Since such a user can be potentially an Employee as well as Contractor, qualifying flags are also present in this table for informational purposes.
The grain of this table is at a single 'User' level. This table is designed to be a slowly/moderately changing dimension that supports Type-2 changes out of the box.

MAPPING.DESCRIPTION:
This mapping adjusts the effective-to date of the historical record in the event of a new record getting inserted because of a Type2 changed being noted in the preceding load process of the Type2 dimension table W_USER_D. Moreover, if any Type1 changes happened, this mapping can also update all the historical records with that change, if configured to behave like that.
There is no update strategy transformation used in this mapping. The session-side parameter "Treat source rows as" will be set to "Update" to take care of this.
MAPPING.NAME: SIL_UserDimension_SCDUpdate

TRANSFORMATION.DESCRIPTION:
This SQL override gets the non-history-tracking columns as well as a few of the system columns from the Type2 dimension table W_USER_D. For each set of natural key (INTEGRATION_ID) and DATASOURCE_NUM_ID, the following logic is used to identify the actual records to be selected:
For the records that were touched in the preceeding load process, did they have history ?
If not (like the case when a simple Type1 change might have occured), the record is not selected.
If it did have history and we need to update all historical records (per mapping parameter $$UPDATE_ALL_HISTORY) with the Type1 changes that might have happened today, all the historical records are selected. Otherwise (where we do not worry about updating all historical records for Type1 changes and just worry about updating the effective date and CURRENT_FLG information in the old record), only the most recent of the historical records is selected.
In either of the cases, the most recent (current) record (which was inserted today probably because of a Type2 changed being noted) will be selected. The final recordset is retured in a descending order of natural key (INTEGRATION_ID), DATASOURCE_NUM_ID and EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT values.
TRANSFORMATION.NAME: Sq_W_USER_D_MX_MOD

TABLEATTRIBUTE.NAME: Sql Query
TABLEATTRIBUTE.VALUE: SELECT TARGET_TABLE.ROW_WID, TARGET_TABLE.FIRST_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.MID_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.LAST_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.FULL_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.NAME_PREFIX, TARGET_TABLE.NAME_SUFFIX, TARGET_TABLE.NAME_EFF_DATE, TARGET_TABLE.SEX_MF_CODE, TARGET_TABLE.SEX_MF_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.ST_ADDRESS, TARGET_TABLE.CITY, TARGET_TABLE.COUNTY, TARGET_TABLE.STATE_CODE, TARGET_TABLE.STATE_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.STATE_REGION, TARGET_TABLE.COUNTRY_CODE, TARGET_TABLE.COUNTRY_NAME, TARGET_TABLE.COUNTRY_REGION, TARGET_TABLE.ZIPCODE, TARGET_TABLE.POST_OFFICE_BOX, TARGET_TABLE.ADDR_EFF_DATE, TARGET_TABLE.ALTERNATE_EMAIL_ADDR, TARGET_TABLE.WEB_ADDRESS, TARGET_TABLE.USER_FORMED_DT, TARGET_TABLE.EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT, TARGET_TABLE.EFFECTIVE_TO_DT, TARGET_TABLE.CURRENT_FLG, TARGET_TABLE.W_UPDATE_DT, TARGET_TABLE.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID, TARGET_TABLE.ETL_PROC_WID, TARGET_TABLE.INTEGRATION_ID, TARGET_TABLE.X_CUSTOM FROM W_USER_D TARGET_TABLE, (SELECT SCD_OUTER.INTEGRATION_ID, SCD_OUTER.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID FROM W_USER_D SCD_OUTER, (SELECT DELTA_OUTER.INTEGRATION_ID, DELTA_OUTER.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID FROM W_USER_D DELTA_OUTER WHERE DELTA_OUTER.ETL_PROC_WID = $$ETL_PROC_WID ) DELTA_TABLE WHERE SCD_OUTER.INTEGRATION_ID = DELTA_TABLE.INTEGRATION_ID AND SCD_OUTER.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID = DELTA_TABLE.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID GROUP BY SCD_OUTER.INTEGRATION_ID, SCD_OUTER.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ) SCD_HISTORY WHERE TARGET_TABLE.INTEGRATION_ID = SCD_HISTORY.INTEGRATION_ID AND TARGET_TABLE.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID = SCD_HISTORY.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID AND TARGET_TABLE.CURRENT_FLG = (CASE WHEN '$$UDATE_ALL_HISTORY' = 'Y' THEN CURRENT_FLG ELSE 'Y' END) ORDER BY TARGET_TABLE.INTEGRATION_ID, TARGET_TABLE.DATASOURCE_NUM_ID, TARGET_TABLE.EFFECTIVE_FROM_DT DESC

TRANSFORMATION.DESCRIPTION:
This expression transformation assigns new values to the Type1 columns (based on the parameter value of $$UPDATE_ALL_HISTORY) as well as stamps the correct values of EFFECTIVE_TO_DT and the CURRENT_FLG for historical records.
This is a 'group' operation and each 'group' is formed by concatenating columns like: INTEGRATION_ID || '~' || TO_CHAR(DATASOURCE_NUM_ID)
TRANSFORMATION.NAME: Exp_W_USER_D_Scd_Update

TRANSFORMATION.DESCRIPTION: This filter transformation stops the most recent (current) record from being processed. Since the data set was ordered descending on natural keys, datasource_num_id and effective_from_dt, the most recent (current) record will always be the first one, and hence, get the REC_NUMBER value = 1.
TRANSFORMATION.NAME: Fil_W_USER_D_Scd_Update
